title: You Tried to Quit… So Why Are You Still Going Back?
paragraphs:
You Tried to Quit… So Why Are You Still Going Back?
The Hidden Reason Willpower Fails Against Sexual Sin—and the Only Way Freedom Actually Begins
You promised yourself this would be the last time.

No more late nights.
No more secret scrolling.
No more “just one more look.”
You said it with conviction. You even prayed. Maybe you cried.
But here you are again… staring at the same screen, carrying the same shame, whispering the same exhausted words:
“Why can’t I stop?”
And the truth that most people are too afraid to say out loud is this…
Willpower alone was never designed to break what your soul is secretly feeding on.
Because this isn’t just a habit.
It’s a hunger.
And hunger doesn’t disappear just because you try harder.
Somewhere deep inside, beyond the behavior, beyond the screen, beyond the moment—you’re reaching for something.
Not just pleasure.
Comfort. Escape. Control. Validation. Relief.
The kind of relief that makes the noise in your mind go quiet for just a few minutes.
But what feels like relief is slowly becoming chains.
And the more you fight it with willpower alone, the more it feels like you’re losing.
Scripture doesn’t ignore this struggle. It exposes it with surgical precision.
In Romans 7:18–19, the apostle Paul writes:
In the original Greek, he uses the word θέλω (thelō)—meaning “to desire, to wish, to intend.”
You want to stop. Your intentions are real.
But then he contrasts it with κατεργάζομαι (katergazomai)—“to produce, to accomplish, to perform.”
Your desire is present… but your ability is broken.
That’s the gap willpower cannot bridge.
Because sin is not just something you do.
It’s something that has learned how to live in you.
Jesus said something that most people read—but don’t fully feel.
“Everyone who commits sin is a slave to sin.” (John 8:34)
The word He used for “slave” in Greek is δοῦλος (doulos)—not just someone who struggles…
…but someone under ownership.
That hits differently when you realize what you’re actually fighting.
This isn’t just a bad habit.
It’s a form of spiritual captivity.
And no slave frees himself by trying harder.
This is why behavior-only solutions keep failing you.
Blocking apps. Cold showers. Self-discipline routines.
They’re not useless—but they’re not enough.
Because you’re trying to cut off fruit… without addressing the root.
And Jesus goes straight to the root.
In Matthew 5:28, He says:
“Everyone who looks at a woman with lustful intent has already committed adultery with her in his heart.”
The word for “lustful intent” is ἐπιθυμέω (epithymeō)—a deep craving, a consuming desire.
This isn’t surface-level attraction.
It’s internal appetite.
And appetite doesn’t die through suppression.
It transforms through replacement.
That’s why David didn’t pray, “God, give me stronger willpower.”
He prayed something far deeper:
“Create in me a clean heart, O God…” (Psalm 51:10)
The Hebrew word for “create” is בָּרָא (bara)—the same word used in Genesis when God created the world out of nothing.
David understood something most people miss:
You don’t need better habits first.
You need a new heart.
And this is where everything changes.
Because Jesus didn’t come just to tell you to stop sinning.
He came to break the power behind the sin.
“Walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh.” (Galatians 5:16)
Notice the order.
Not: “Stop the flesh so you can walk in the Spirit.”
But: “Walk in the Spirit… and the flesh loses its grip.”
The word “walk” in Greek is περιπατέω (peripateō)—to live daily, step by step.
This isn’t a one-time decision.
It’s a daily dependence.
A surrender.
A relationship.
Because the real battle was never just about what you’re doing with your body.
It’s about who is leading your soul.
And willpower makes you the leader.
But the Gospel invites you to surrender that position.
You don’t overcome sexual sin by becoming stronger.
You overcome it by becoming surrendered.
That’s why some of you feel stuck…
Because you’ve been trying to fix this privately.
Silently.
Independently.
But freedom was never designed to grow in isolation.
And maybe this is the moment where honesty finally breaks through.
Not fake strength.
Not hidden struggle.
But real, raw confession.
Because healing begins where hiding ends.
Be honest.
This hit deeper than you expected.
Someone you love is silently losing this same battle.
They smile in public… but fight in private.
Not to expose them—but to reach them.
Because if you truly want to glorify God with your life…
You don’t just consume truth.
You help spread it.
It’s about getting truth like this in front of more souls who are drowning silently.
If your spirit knows it’s time to grow…
Because this isn’t just about quitting a habit.
It’s about becoming a new creation.
“Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation…” (2 Corinthians 5:17)
The old patterns don’t define you.
The old failures don’t own you.
And the old version of you is not your final story.
You are not too far gone.
You are not too addicted.
You are not too broken.
Jesus didn’t come for the version of you that already has it together.
He came for the one still struggling… still falling… still reaching.
And He’s not done with you yet.
You don’t need stronger willpower.
You need a surrendered heart—and a living Savior.
And He’s already calling your name.
Right here.
Right now.
Don’t ignore it this time.
You kept calling it a habit… but heaven has been calling it a rescue mission.
